audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows argued against their own why-text. Level 1 was Jax while whys[0] calls it a 'dead stage for both'; levels 4-5 and First item were Skill while whys[3] says 'he wins every extended trade' and whys[5] says his first-item spike 'still out-duels you'; 2+ items was Jax while whys[6] and late both say Kayle takes over.
audit.why: At level 1 both have one point and melee autos. From 2 to first item Counter Strike's dodge-and-stun plus Grandmaster-at-Arms resists win every extended trade. At two items Kayle is ranged and kites outside Leap Strike's 700.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group — the same rows the Jax-side audit flipped — with ratings inverted and all four phases[].why lines rewritten.
sources: brief currentText whys[0], whys[3], whys[5], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is named as the tracked cooldown in twelve places with no number, so 'engage when it's down' had no duration attached.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — 17s at rank 1 is a long window and the whole reason a farming Kayle gets any free autos at all. Leap Strike's 700 range is the spacing number for the late game.
audit.corrected: 17s written into phases[3].why, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t; Leap Strike's 700 range into phases[6].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. The page never said what Counter Strike actually dodges — Riot's text is 'dodge all incoming attacks', i.e. basic attacks, so Radiant Blast still lands through it. And nothing mentioned that Empower is an auto-attack reset, so the reader has no tell for when the burst is coming.
audit.why: A Kayle who knows her Q lands through Counter Strike keeps her shred and slow up during his dodge window; a Kayle who reads the Empower wind-up steps out before the hit rather than after it.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states Counter Strike dodges autos, not Radiant Blast — matching the Jax-side audit. dontsFull[1].d now gives the Empower reset wind-up as the step-back cue.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Leap Strikes' in early; it is Leap Strike used as a verb ('Jax Q Leap Strikes onto you'), not a wrong name, so the line was left alone.

edits.before: You are the weakest level 1 in the game — pay rent quietly. Identify how Jax contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Dead stage — one ability point each and melee autos both ways, so nobody owns level 1. Take the safe CS and bleed nothing.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Counter Strike (17s at rank 1) dodges your autos and stuns — he wins every extended trade until you go ranged, so farm safe.

edits.before: Nashor's Tooth is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Counter Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: His first item plus R resists still out-duel you — kite and scale, do not force the fight yet.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Jax carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Ranged Starfire waves out-DPS his melee and you kite outside Leap Strike (700) — the finite duelist falls off.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Respect it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — step up only when it is down.

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Respect it. When it is down — E-poke + scale.
edits.after: Track Counter Strike (17s): it dodges autos, not Radiant Blast. When it is down — E-poke and scale.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His combo opens on an Empower reset — step back at the wind-up.

notes: Same four rows the Jax-side audit flipped, flipped here with inverse ratings, so both directions now read Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Kayle. Every flipped row already had prose arguing for its new side. Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only per Riot's text, so Radiant Blast lands through it — now stated on both pages. Kayle's level 11 / 16 form breakpoints are the real scaling clock but the kit file gives no level numbers, so the page's 'first item / two items' framing was left as the proxy rather than invented around.
